questions.q: Which Cosmos DB API is the native API?
options: Core (SQL) API
MongoDB API
Cassandra API
Table API
questions.explain: Core (SQL) API stores JSON documents and queries with a SQL-like dialect — it's Cosmos DB's original, first-class interface.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which API should a brand-new project with no existing codebase choose?
options: Core (SQL) API, because it's native and every feature lands there first, sometimes exclusively
Whichever API the developer happens to be personally most familiar with
The Table API, because it's the simplest
It doesn't matter — all five APIs have identical feature parity
questions.explain: The lesson gives an honest, direct recommendation: Core API for new projects, since the other APIs are compatibility layers with real constraints.

questions.q: What protocol does the Gremlin API implement?
options: The Apache TinkerPop Gremlin graph traversal language
The MongoDB wire protocol
Cassandra Query Language (CQL)
The Azure Table Storage API
questions.explain: Gremlin API exposes graph traversal via nodes and edges, implementing the Apache TinkerPop Gremlin language.

questions.q: Why do the MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, and Table APIs exist on Cosmos DB, per this lesson?
options: For migration compatibility — letting existing applications and drivers move onto Cosmos DB's engine with less code rewrite
Because Core API doesn't actually work and these are the real APIs
They exist purely for marketing purposes with no functional difference
Microsoft requires all five APIs to be used together on every project
questions.explain: These APIs are wire-protocol compatibility layers that ease migration for teams already invested in those ecosystems.

questions.q: What real constraint do the non-Core APIs carry, according to this lesson?
options: They don't always expose 100% feature parity with their native counterpart, since they translate a protocol onto Cosmos DB's own underlying model
They are slower than Core API in every single case with no exceptions
They cannot be used in production environments
They require a completely separate Cosmos DB account type
questions.explain: Because these APIs translate another database's wire protocol onto Cosmos DB's document/partition model, they aren't ground-up native implementations.
